metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Pressure and Archimedes' Principle — Caribbean Sea Context
metadata.caribbean_note: Questions set in the Caribbean Sea; diver depth and floating boat scenarios

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q4 — Liquid Pressure and Archimedes
question.text:
This question uses two scenarios involving the Caribbean Sea (density of sea water ρ = 1 025 kg m⁻³, g = 10 N kg⁻¹).

Part A: A diver is at a depth of 0.5 km below the surface of the Caribbean Sea.

Part B: A boat with a weight of 83 000 N floats in the same sea water.
question.general_feedback:
Part A — Liquid pressure:
P = ρgh = 1025 × 10 × 500 = 5 125 000 Pa (= 5.125 × 10⁶ Pa)

Part B — Volume displaced:
Upthrust = weight = 83 000 N → mass displaced = 83000/10 = 8300 kg → V = m/ρ = 8300/1025 = 8.10 m³

steps.label:
Given: ρsea water = 1 025 kg m⁻³  |  g = 10 N kg⁻¹
Formulas: P = ρgh    Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced    ρ = m/V
Part A — Calculate the liquid pressure on a diver at 0.5 km depth. (4 marks)
Part B — A boat (weight = 83 000 N) floats in sea water. Calculate the volume of sea water displaced. (5 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: P = ρgh = 1025 × 10 × 500. Check you converted 0.5 km to 500 m first.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use P = ρgh (not P = F/A here — we are calculating liquid pressure at depth).

fields.label: Upthrust on the floating boat = _____ N
fields.diagnostic_hint: A floating object: upthrust = weight of object = 83 000 N (Archimedes' principle)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: For a floating object, upthrust equals the weight of the object. So upthrust = 83 000 N.

fields.label: Mass of sea water displaced = _____ kg
fields.diagnostic_hint: Upthrust = m × g → m = Upthrust / g = 83000 / 10 = 8300 kg

fields.label: Volume of sea water displaced V = _____ m³

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use ρ = m/V rearranged to V = m/ρ
